P0 FOLLOW-UP: not a regression. The 15-minute hold is COMPACT-ON-CLOSE, and the incident's own
commit timeline proves the lock was acquired AFTER the verifier finished, not during it.

## The incident, from the tracker's commit log
pid 61327 was closing `repressive-delectable-swan` = 271c-e88f-3220-4c9b. Tracker commits:

    20:35:43  COMPLETION_VERDICT 271c   <- LLM verification FINISHED (sidecar written)
    20:35:47  STATUS            271c    <- the close itself (txn.transition_core)
    20:35:49  SIGNATURE         271c    <- PASS attestation signed
    20:35:52  .ticket-write.lock.d created   <- the hold you observed begins
    ...13m53s...
    20:49:45  COMPACT           271c    <- compact-on-close commits; lock released

The lock dir was born 3 seconds AFTER the SIGNATURE commit and 9 seconds after the verifier's
COMPLETION_VERDICT. One continuous hold, one ctime — exactly as observed — but its span is
`_compact_on_close`, not the verify phase. The verify phase held nothing.

## The same shape on every other close that hour
    f6e9: STATUS 20:20:01  SIGNATURE 20:20:04  COMPACT 20:22:31  -> 2m27s locked
    594b: STATUS 20:32:27  SIGNATURE 20:32:29  COMPACT 20:34:56  -> 2m27s locked
    271c: STATUS 20:35:47  SIGNATURE 20:35:49  COMPACT 20:49:45  -> 13m56s locked  (the incident)
    8fc2: STATUS 20:51:54  SIGNATURE 20:51:56  COMPACT 20:54:37  -> 2m41s locked

8fc2 was captured LIVE while investigating: `ls` of the lock dir at 20:54:35 showed stamp
`pid=85578`, a `rebar transition ... in_progress closed --ref c392d736` that had been running
4m27s and had held the lock since 20:51:59 — i.e. the same post-verify compaction span.

## Instrumented confirmation on current main (70679d3c21)
Two probes, both on the real close path:
- Wrapping `_store.lock.acquire` / `LockHandle.release` around a full `transition_compute`
  close shows exactly four acquisitions, ALL after the verifier returns, each bracketing only a
  store mutation: completion sidecar append, `txn.transition_core`, SIGNATURE append,
  `_compact_on_close`.
- A faithful sleeping-stub repro (stubbing only the innermost
  `llm.workflow.gate_dispatch.produce_completion_verdict`, so the REAL `verify_completion`
  wrapper still runs — snapshot handle resolution, `materialize_tickets`, `gate_read_root`)
  with a background thread sampling the lock dir every 20ms for the whole close:
  112 samples, 0 with the lock present during the verify phase; four post-verify holds of
  25ms, 25ms, 0ms, 48ms.

None of the seven listed commits (64451ec0bb, 61b49deaa6, 8f6b6c9356, 61058f6085, cc69cc1179,
746c1ba2e9, e0b3fdfc8e) moved acquisition ahead of the verifier. The verifier has run outside
the lock since the gate was introduced in 85a77b9cc8 (2026-06-18); `git log -S` over
transition.py / transition_close.py / close_precheck.py finds no commit that ever placed it
inside. There is no regression to revert.

## Why the stand-aside guard does not help
`_compact_on_close` probes `write_lock_is_busy` and skips when busy (bug 7084 / R3). That guard
cannot fire for the CLOSING process: the close released the lock microseconds earlier
(SIGNATURE at 20:35:49, probe at ~20:35:52), so the store reads free and compaction takes it.
7084 measured this holder at 48.1s; on today's 745M / ~4000-ticket store it is 2.5-14 minutes,
and it scales with store size. The lock-retry work (REBAR_LOCK_RETRIES, cc69cc1179) raises the
waiter's budget but cannot shorten a 14-minute holder.

## Scope
Fixing this changes WHEN compaction runs (skip / defer out-of-band / bound the lock-held
portion) — a user-visible change to close semantics beyond "move verification outside the
lock", which is already true. Raised separately as `choosy-arthrodic-barbet`
(cfcb-a023-09a0-42ad, linked discovered_from). Requesting a scope decision: re-point THIS
ticket at the compaction holder, or close it as not-a-bug (premise falsified) and run the fix
on choosy-arthrodic-barbet.
